propositions: When a claim gate configured as ATTESTED cannot resolve its gate ref (origin/main), the freshness re-check silently substitutes the in-place working tree as the hashing basis via a broad `except Exception` in `_hash_basis`, causing fail-OPEN (claim certified) instead of fail-CLOSED (claim blocked).

`gate_ref_hash_basis` returns a `GateRefBasis` object with `.degraded=True` flag when substitution occurs, but the claim-gate verifier in `compute_validity` ignores this signal and certifies against the substituted basis.

The defect violates documented fail-closed contracts (plan-review-gate.md, ADR 0002) and affects production (deployed MCP box, review-bot), where ref resolution can fail due to missing remotes, failed blob top-up, or transient git faults.

When gate ref is resolvable, drift is correctly detected as `stale-code` and claim is blocked; when gate ref is unresolvable and working tree matches signed content, the same claim is incorrectly certified as `ok=True/certified`.

The fix wires the claim-gate verifier to consume the `.degraded` signal and return `stale-code` verdict (named with the unobtainable ref) instead of comparing hashes against the substituted working tree, while preserving `_hash_basis` contract and exempting `source=local` gates.
